datasource_item.last_query_text: How do I ask for an extension on a problem set?
datasource_item.sample.output_text:
Here’s a practical way to ask for an extension, plus ready-to-use templates you can adapt.

Key tips
- Ask early. Don’t wait until the last minute.
- Check the course policy first (late policies, allowable extensions, any forms).
- Be specific. Propose a new deadline you can meet.
- Show progress. Mention what you’ve completed and what remains.
- Keep it concise and respectful. Acknowledge you understand extensions aren’t always possible.
- Offer alternatives if an extension isn’t allowed (partial submission, different assignment, etc.).

What to include in your message
- A clear subject line (if email)
- A brief greeting
- A short reason for the request (without oversharing)
- A proposed new deadline
- What you’ve already completed and your plan to finish
- Acknowledgement of policy and appreciation

Templates

1) Formal email to professor
Subject: Request for extension on Problem Set [number] for [Course name]

Dear Professor [Last Name],

I hope you’re well. I am writing to request a short extension for Problem Set [number], which is currently due on [original due date].

The reason for this request is [brief reason, e.g., a heavy workload this week / illness / a personal matter]. I want to ensure I can submit work that reflects my best effort. If possible, could the deadline be extended to [proposed new due date]?

So far, I have completed [briefly describe progress, e.g., problems 1–3 and part of 4] and plan to complete [what remains] by the extended date. If an extension isn’t possible, I will submit by the original deadline, but I would be grateful for any alternative you might suggest (e.g., partial credit for the portion completed).

Thank you for considering this request.

Best regards,
[Your Name]
[Course and section]
[Student ID] (optional)

2) Short/concise message to TA or via course platform
Hi [TA’s name], I’m requesting a short extension for Problem Set [number], due [date]. Due to [reason], I’d be able to submit by [new date]. I’ve completed [brief progress]. If an extension isn’t possible, I’ll submit by the original deadline. Thanks for considering.

3) In-person or quick chat
“Hey Professor [Last Name], do you have a moment? I wanted to ask about possibly getting a brief extension on Problem Set [number]. I’m behind a bit due to [reason], and I think I could produce a stronger submission if I could move the due date to [new date]. I’ve already completed [brief progress]. I understand if extensions aren’t possible, but I wanted to check.”

If you have documentation
- If you have a medical note or official documentation, mention you can provide it if needed.
- Keep a simple line: “I can share documentation if that would help.”

What to avoid
- Don’t push for extensions repeatedly or after being denied.
- Don’t fabricate reasons; be honest.
- Don’t imply you’ll do worse unless you’re granted more time.
- Don’t demand a specific outcome; be polite and flexible.

If an extension is denied
- Ask about the policy for partial credit or alternative assignments.
- Consider requesting a smaller extension or a revised deadline for a subset of the problems.
- Plan to submit by the original deadline with the best quality you can achieve.

If you want, tell me your course, assignment details, and your reason. I can tailor a precise email for you.
